Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates complete opacification of the left hemithorax with significant volume loss (mediastinal shift to the left, elevated left hemidiaphragm) and marked compensatory hyperinflation (radiolucency) of the right lung. While total atelectasis causes similar ipsilateral findings, the profound contralateral overinflation is a hallmark adaptive change in pulmonary aplasia where the remaining lung develops to fill the thoracic cavity due to congenital absence of the affected lung tissue. *(guided by t000002)*
